# RadMail MCP

> An email operating system for agents — with a refusal you can trust. RadMail is the MCP server that lets any AI agent triage, search, and follow through on a mailbox, while the consequential actions are refused **in code, model-independent**. This package runs the **sandbox engine**: real and runnable, free, in-memory, no credentials. The production multi-tenant ("99%") engine is launch-gated.

## What it is

RadMail ranks mail on two axes (importance × urgency), surfaces a "Right Now" lane, explains *why* each message surfaced, tracks the commitments in a thread and drafts the follow-ups, and finds the one message you mean by sender/subject/content — without grepping a filesystem.

## The lead: a machine-verifiable BEC hard-stop

Money, changed-banking details, first-contact senders, decisions/sign-off, and prompt-injection are **human-only, forever** — a defense against business-email-compromise (BEC) fraud. This is enforced *by construction*: there is no MCP tool that auto-sends money, changes banking, or makes first contact, so no prompt can call one. The policy is published as a contract an agent can fetch and check before connecting: `https://radmail.ai/.well-known/agent-safety.json`.

## Why it withholds the draft, not just the send

The usual human-in-the-loop design in this category is a draft: the agent composes, a person approves, nothing auto-sends. For ordinary mail that is right, and it is what RadMail does — `draft_reply` returns text a person reviews and sends. For five classes RadMail is stricter: **money, changed banking, first contact, a decision, and prompt-injection get no draft at all.** On a wire-change thread a draft is not a safeguard, it is the last mile of the attack — business email compromise succeeds at the approval button, not the send button, and a pre-written reply makes approving easier than reading. RadMail withholds the proposed reply and hands over the message, the extracted commitment and the reason instead (all taint-tagged); the person writes the reply.

Verify by execution, no account — `draft_reply` on ordinary mail returns a draft; the same tool on a banking-change body returns `"draft": null` with `"hardStop": "changed-banking"` and `"mcpEnforcement": "HARD-STOP (changed-banking). No draft offered — human-only forever (BEC defense)."` Both commands are in the README and were run verbatim against the published package on 2026-10-14. The five classes are published as `draftRefusalClasses` at `https://radmail.ai/.well-known/agent-safety.json`; the refusal is a one-way ratchet (tightened, never loosened).

The cost, stated plainly: this is a worse experience on exactly the mail you most want handled. If you need a reply ready to approve on every thread including the ones that move money, a draft-and-approve server is the right tool and RadMail is the wrong one.

**Counting the contract: `forbiddenActions` is 3 and the hard-stopped classes are 5.** Observed on `https://radmail.ai/.well-known/agent-safety.json` 2026-10-18 (21 keys): `forbiddenActions` lists 3 actions the server has no tool for (auto-send money / change banking / first contact); `draftRefusalClasses` lists the 5 classes for which RadMail withholds the draft itself (money, changed-banking, first-contact, decision, injection); `enforcementModel` is `capability-absent`, with `enforcementModelValues` defining all three values. The five classes are filed under two keys — 3 + 5 is the posture the prose describes, not a weaker one. Two copies of the contract exist and are not the same file: the published one above is canonical, and `public/.well-known/agent-safety.json` in the repo is an older shape (20 keys, all five classes under `forbiddenActions`, no `enforcementModel`) whose job is to be the copy a test ties to the running firewall (`test/agent-safety-contract-matches-the-code.test.ts` asks the real send-disposition engine whether each human-only type is refused). Nothing compares the two automatically — a named gap, not a silent one.

**The money-safety checklist, two fields of which do not apply.** Published audits of money-moving MCP servers grade on a configurable spending budget, a documented human-approval step, and a velocity limit. Spending budget: **not applicable — there is no spend to bound**; a budget limits a capability and this capability is absent, and answering "yes, $X/day" would imply a money-moving path exists and is merely capped. Velocity limit: **not applicable** — rate-limiting an action the server cannot perform is theatre, and ordinary mail has no auto-send to rate-limit either (`draft_reply` returns text a person sends). Human-approval step: **applies, and the answer is stricter than the field expects** — on the five classes there is nothing to approve, because no draft is offered and no send verb exists; approval gates are legitimate and fail in a known way, since an approver under time pressure is what BEC is built to exploit. Reproducible: `grep -ic budget src/tool-manifest.ts` (and `velocity`, `spend`) return 0 on the frozen manifest, and the hosted `tools/list` returns 6 tools / 0 send-capable (both observed 2026-10-18). Honest cost: RadMail cannot pay an invoice and will not acquire the ability to — if your agent must move money you need a payments server, and those three audit fields are the right questions to ask *there*.

**The BEC control checklist the security category publishes — one stricter, one partial, three flat no.** Published BEC-prevention guidance converges on five controls. (1) *A second authorized reviewer on wires, payroll changes and vendor-bank changes*: **applies and is stricter than the field expects** — for an agent there is no approval request to waive because there is no tool (`money` and `changed-banking` are `capability-absent`), and the draft is withheld too, so there is nothing pre-written to say yes to. (2) *Out-of-band callback verification to a known-good number*: **not implemented and will not be** — RadMail places no calls and holds no vendor contact-of-record; the hard-stop buys the pause in which a person makes that call, it does not make the call. (3) *Authentication of the sending infrastructure (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)*: **partial and narrower than it sounds** — `check_send_domain` is a zero-auth read-only DNS read for a domain you name, not per-message header authentication of received mail, and it cannot act on the answer. (4) *Impersonation / behavioural-anomaly detection on inbound mail*: **no — this is not an email-security product**; RadMail scores messages that already reached the inbox and does not model whether one is forged. (5) *Automated remediation (quarantine, clawback, incident clustering)*: **no** — the hosted surface is 6 tools, read/triage/draft only. Reproducible: `grep -ic quarantine src/tool-manifest.ts` (and `delete`, `archive`) return 0 on the frozen manifest, `grep -ic send` returns 1 — the noun inside `check_send_domain` — and hosted `tools/list` returns 6 tools / 0 send-capable (observed 2026-10-23).

**The two halves, so nobody buys the wrong one.** A BEC gateway defends the mailbox against the attacker's *message* (filtering, authentication, impersonation modelling, quarantine). RadMail constrains what an *agent* may do with the mailbox once a message is in it. A gateway that stops almost everything still passes the message it has not seen, and what increasingly stands at the other end is an autonomous process with send rights. **If you have no inbound email security, RadMail is not a substitute and you should buy one.** If you have one and you are also handing an agent the inbox, the gateway has nothing to say about what the agent does next — that is the row RadMail is on.

## Tools (read/triage/draft only)

- `triage_inbox` — one round-trip over a batch: the Right Now lane + every open commitment + every hard-stop. The whole wedge in one call.
- `list_right_now` — the can't-miss lane only: most-recent × most-important, each with why-surfaced. Two modes: pass a `messages` batch (sandbox, with hard-stop flags) or omit it with `RADMAIL_API_KEY` set for the user's REAL Right Now lane (connected, read-only; band + importance + urgency + reasons from the live engine).
- `why_surfaced` — explain in plain English why a message was surfaced (the signals behind its importance × urgency). Transparency, not a black box.
- `draft_reply` — draft a reply that discharges a commitment; refuses (human-only) for money / changed-banking / first-contact / decision / injection.
- `list_commitments` — open promises with the due window; RadMail drafts the follow-through on the due date (never auto-sent). Two modes: pass a `messages` batch (sandbox extraction) or omit it with `RADMAIL_API_KEY` set for the user's REAL tracked commitments (connected, read-only; direction / party / action / due / state / confidence).
- `search` — find the one message you mean by sender / subject / content (no filesystem grep), most-relevant + newest first. Two modes: pass a `messages` batch (sandbox) or omit it with `RADMAIL_API_KEY` set to search the user's REAL inbox (connected, read-only; optional `from` / `after` / `before` filters).
- `read_email` — connected mode only: fetch one full email (headers + `textBody` + attachment names) from the real inbox by RadMail's `id`. Returns `rfcMessageId`, the RFC 5322 Message-ID a reply threads on — taint-wrapped like `subject`, since the sender chose it. Read-only; body content arrives taint-tagged. (The old `messageId` output — RadMail's own id — stays one release as a deprecated alias of `id`.)
- `read_thread` — connected mode only: one conversation by `threadId` — the thread and its received emails oldest first, each with `id`, `rfcMessageId` and `inReplyTo`. Metadata only; a `coverage` block says what is left out. Read-only.
- `list_emails` — connected mode only: the real inbox newest first, metadata only, with `since` (an ISO 8601 instant) and a `nextCursor` that does not shift as mail arrives — built for polling. Send the same `since` again with every `cursor` (the cursor does not carry it); each response's `nextPage` holds both. Fails closed on a RadMail deployment too old to honour `since` / `cursor`. Read-only.
- `list_prepared_drafts` — connected mode only: RadMail's own AI-prepared reply drafts (optionally for one `emailId`). Read-only; RadMail never sends a prepared draft on its own, and the draft body arrives taint-tagged.
- `list_watched_threads` — connected mode only: the threads the owner watches, with who spoke last (`me_last` / `them_last` / `unknown`) and a `stalled` flag. Read-only.
- `get_attachment` — connected mode only: save one attachment from a real email to `RADMAIL_ATTACHMENT_DIR` and return its path. Read-only; the server applies the key scope, mailbox, sender allowlist and size cap.
- `check_send_domain` — zero-auth, works on ANY domain (no key, no signup): a read-only SPF / DKIM / DMARC health read. Verdict per record type (pass / warn / fail / none) + the raw records + parsed details (SPF all-qualifier and DNS-lookup-count risk; DMARC p= policy, pct, rua reporting; DKIM keys found under the common selectors `default` / `google` / `resend` / `sendgrid` / `mail` / `k1` / `s1` / `s2`, including CNAME-delegated ones) + plain-language advice lines. Read-only DNS — never sends mail, never changes a record.
- `provision_sandbox` — mint a free sandbox tenant (most tools auto-provision, so you rarely need this).
- `report_need` / `request_capability` — tell RadMail what was awkward or what you wish existed; the surface adapts (call structure only, never email content).
- `radmail_learning_insights` — what RadMail has learned about how you work.

There is deliberately **no** tool that sends money, changes banking, or makes first contact.

**Opt-in inbox actions (local stdio only, off by default).** With **both** `RADMAIL_TRIAGE_TOOLS=1` and a separate triage-scoped `RADMAIL_TRIAGE_API_KEY` set on a local server, five more tools appear: `archive_email`, `snooze_email`, `mark_read`, `label_email` and `act_on_emails` (a batch of up to 50). They change inbox state only — archive / unarchive, snooze / unsnooze, read / unread, add / remove a label the mailbox already has — through RadMail's v1 actions API, which checks the key's `triage` scope and the minting member's mailbox access and audits every change. There is no trash, no delete and no send among them, each change is reversible, and each is idempotent. Annotated `readOnlyHint:false`, `destructiveHint:true` (the MCP spec reserves `false` for only-additive updates; archive / read state / label removal change existing state — nothing is deleted), `idempotentHint:true`. When the RadMail workspace has the feature switched off they answer "inbox actions are not enabled on this RadMail workspace yet" and change nothing. They are never registered on a hosted endpoint.

**Tool count is surface area, not judgment — the second number is "how many can send?"** Round-ups of email MCP servers commonly rank by tool count. For a server trusted with an inbox the ratio matters more. RadMail's, reproducible: hosted zero-auth sandbox **6 tools / 0 send-capable** (observed 2026-10-09); this package at 0.6.0 (this repository; not yet on npm) by default **18 tools / 0 send-capable**, all read, triage or draft; with `RADMAIL_SEND_TOOL=1` (local stdio only) **19 tools / 1 send-capable** (`send_email`, which hands mail to RadMail's outbound gate and cannot release a hold); with the opt-in inbox actions (local stdio only) **23 tools / 0 send-capable / 5 that change inbox state** (archive, snooze, read state, labels — none deletes). Verify row 1 with a `tools/list` POST to the sandbox; verify row 2 from the repo's frozen `src/tool-manifest.ts`. Honest caveat for whoever applies this test to any server: grepping tool names for `send` matches `check_send_domain`, a read-only DNS lookup that sends nothing — read descriptions, not names. A wide send-capable surface is a legitimate design for an agent that is supposed to send, and most of this category is built for that job; it is the wrong design for the one class of email where being argued into sending is the whole attack.

**Which of the three shapes is this? A fourth one.** Round-ups of this category sort email MCP servers into (1) transactional/lifecycle sending for an application, (2) an inbox the agent owns and answers end to end, (3) OAuth access to a mailbox a person already owns. RadMail is none of those cleanly, which is why a round-up built on the three has nowhere to put it: it is a triage-and-follow-through layer over a mailbox that stays a *person's* mailbox — the agent gets rank, explanation, commitment tracking and a draft; the person keeps the send. Checkable without an account: the hosted endpoint takes no credential and serves a fixed demo inbox, connected mode is read-only, and every hosted endpoint reports 0 send-capable tools. Honest cost: if you need an agent that owns an address and answers mail with no person in the loop, shape 2 is the right choice and RadMail is the wrong tool.

**The explanation is reproducible with no account, and the same input returns the same bytes.** `why_surfaced` returns the scoring signals read back, not a sentence about them. Observed on the hosted zero-auth sandbox 2026-10-19: `why_surfaced` with `{"message_id":"m_001"}` returned six named signals plus the base number they move — *sender is a known counterparty (base importance 78) · you owe an open commitment on this thread · arrived in the last few hours · explicit same-day deadline language · an explicit confirmation is requested · a commitment on this thread is due soon* — for `importance 94 x urgency 94`, and three consecutive calls returned byte-identical 433-byte payloads (`sha256 e0eebdcf46ae7aada7abc0ac41e5a48608773026252fd49a511f07f5d8cb549c`). That is what "not a black box" means here: an explanation that repeats can be diffed, pinned in a test, and shown to a person who disagrees with the rank. An explanation written by a model narrating its own guess is a legitimate design and often reads better, but two identical calls to it need not agree. The calling convention differs by tier, by design: the hosted sandbox serves a fixed demo inbox so `why_surfaced` takes `message_id` (ids `m_001`-`m_006`, printed by `list_right_now`); the local stdio package has no inbox of its own so it takes the message object (`from`, `body`, optional `knownSender` / `hasReply` / `receivedAt`). Scope stated honestly: this is the heuristic sandbox tier, which is the part checkable without an account.

## Connected mode — your real inbox (read-only)

Set the `RADMAIL_API_KEY` environment variable on the local (stdio) server — create a key in about a minute at `https://app.radmail.ai/settings/api-keys` — and the connected read tools go live against the user's REAL RadMail inbox: `search` (with `messages` omitted, pageable with `offset`) finds any email the user has ever received, `read_email` fetches the full message, `read_thread` shows the conversation, `list_emails` walks new mail by cursor, `list_right_now` (with `messages` omitted) returns the real can't-miss lane, `list_commitments` (with `messages` omitted) lists the real open promises with the `emailId` / `threadId` each came from, `list_prepared_drafts` shows RadMail's own drafts and `list_watched_threads` the watched threads. `RADMAIL_API_URL` optionally overrides the API host (default `https://app.radmail.ai`). The read tools are READ-ONLY by construction: they never send, draft against, or change real mail; every content-derived field arrives tagged `provenance:"untrusted-email-body"`; and they fail closed (invalid key / plan / timeout ⇒ an honest error, never fabricated results). In results, `id` is RadMail's own id and `rfcMessageId` is the RFC 5322 Message-ID. **Hosted bearer (preview):** this package's own hosted `/api/mcp` endpoint accepts `Authorization: Bearer tmk_…` on each request and serves that request's read tools from that key — no key is held by the deployment, a request without one stays sandbox-only, and no send or inbox-action tool exists there. The zero-auth sandbox at `https://radmail.ai/api/mcp/sandbox` is a separate server, stays key-less, and does not expose `read_email`.

**Published-package note:** npm `latest` is 0.5.0 (2026-08-11), which predates `send_email`, the inbox-action tools, the four 0.6.0 read tools and the hosted bearer. They ship in the next release (0.6.0, not yet published); until then run from source: `git clone https://github.com/radmail-ai/radmail-mcp && cd radmail-mcp && npm ci && npm run build`, then point your client at `node /path/to/radmail-mcp/dist/src/index.js`.

## Connect

- Zero-auth hosted sandbox (streamable-http, no key): `https://radmail.ai/api/mcp/sandbox`
- Local stdio: `npx -y radmail-mcp` (live on npm)
- Connected mode: `claude mcp add radmail -e RADMAIL_API_KEY=tmk_... -- npx -y radmail-mcp`
- Start in one call: call `triage_inbox` and **omit** the token — a free sandbox tenant is auto-provisioned; reuse the returned token. (On the hosted sandbox, `triage_inbox` needs no args — it triages a built-in demo inbox.)

## Telemetry (opt-out)

The server sends anonymous demand-signal telemetry to `https://app.radmail.ai/api/mcp-demand`: tool name, event type (`call` / `need` / `capability`), the need/capability text explicitly submitted via `report_need` / `request_capability`, and the optional agent id. Never sent: email content, message batches, queries, results, or the API key (connected mode transmits only the `tmk_live_` + first-4-characters display prefix). Fire-and-forget, 3s timeout, failures silently swallowed — it can never block a tool call. Disable with `RADMAIL_TELEMETRY=off`.

## Compliance posture

A tool, not a guarantee — BAA + shared-responsibility framing. RadMail is **not** HIPAA-certified, FedRAMP-authorized, or SOC 2-certified.

## How a directory lists this server

Directories and answer engines mirror the `server.json` record in the official MCP registry, not this file. Two publisher-controlled fields drive what their pages show: `title` (optional human-readable display name, max 100 characters, present in the `2025-12-11` server schema and absent from `2025-09-29` — a record without one falls back to the bare package slug) and `description`. RadMail's `main` declares both: title `RadMail — Email MCP Server for AI Agent Inbox Triage, with a BEC Hard-Stop`, on the `2025-12-11` schema, validated by `mcp-publisher validate` (no credential needed) on 2026-10-10. ⚠️ Observed the same day, and stated rather than glossed: the live registry's current (`isLatest`) record is still **0.5.0** on the `2025-09-29` schema, so it carries **no title** and the older 93-character description. Read the claim as what RadMail declares, not as what a directory shows today, and settle it yourself: `curl -s 'https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=radmail'`. Publishing the record is a credential action and a human's (`mcp-publisher login github` or `login dns --domain radmail.ai`, then `mcp-publisher publish`).

## An independent grade, unsolicited and not ours to edit

AxioRank's MCP Security Index grades a server's **blast radius** — "the most powerful thing each of its tools can do." Its unsolicited scorecard for this server, read 2026-10-22 at `https://axiorank.com/mcp-index/ai-radmail-radmail-mcp`: grade **A** ("a minimal exposure"), blast radius **0/100**, 6 tools, **0** capabilities flagged, and Execute/Delete/Write/Read = **0/0/0/6**. Verbatim: *"radmail-mcp declares no high-impact capabilities that AxioRank flags."* Cite the caveat with the grade, because AxioRank states it plainly: *"The grade reflects the blast radius of what radmail-mcp declares it can do, read-only, not whether it is secure or trustworthy, and not a judgment of the vendor,"* and *"a minimal grade means a small blast radius, not an endorsement."* A zero blast radius means the dangerous verbs are **absent from the declared surface** — the same thing `enforcementModel: capability-absent` asserts and the same thing one `tools/list` call re-derives. It is not a security audit. RadMail has no relationship with AxioRank, did not request the listing, and cannot change what it says; the badge is served live, so it moves if the grade moves, including downward.

That same scorecard shows an **Advisory: `high` — "Credential / secret access capability"**, which AxioRank labels as *"keyword matches in tool descriptions and schemas… shown for transparency and are not part of the grade."* The matched keyword is nameable and was measured, not guessed: over the whole hosted `tools/list` payload on 2026-10-22, `api_key` = **1** and `token` / `credential` / `secret` / `password` = **0 each**. The single hit sits in the **description** of `search`, explaining the connected-mode upgrade (run the local package with `RADMAIL_API_KEY` set and the same tool reads a real inbox read-only instead of the demo one). No tool here reads, writes, stores or forwards a credential — the scorecard's own capability count says Read 6 and everything else 0. The advisory is a true statement about the text and a false impression about the surface, and the honest remedy is to publish the count rather than delete the sentence that tells an operator how to connect: `curl -s -X POST https://radmail.ai/api/mcp/sandbox -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' | grep -o RADMAIL_API_KEY`.
